# 有限视界：任何有限的历史都不决定一段汲取是更新还是消耗 / Finite horizon: no finite history decides whether drawing renews or consumes

## 主张 Claim

在 Becoming.Renewal 的公地过程中，对每个视界 h，有两次运行在 h 之前的配置与动作都相同：焦点形成每一步都汲取两个单位（每步更新一个），而它的每个事件都在更新之内。此后一次在更新之内汲取，焦点形成在运行中是更新的；另一次继续超出，焦点形成是消耗的。因此，任何由前 h 步的配置与动作决定、并记入每次更新运行的读法，必记入某次消耗运行。分类不仅不是初始配置的函数，也不是任何有限前缀的函数。不用伦理前提，也不用 Lean 公理。 / In the commons process of Becoming.Renewal, for every horizon h there are two runs whose configurations and actions agree before h: the focal formation draws two units at every step (one is renewed each step), and each of its events is within renewal. Afterwards one run draws within renewal and the focal formation renews in it; the other keeps exceeding and the focal formation consumes. Hence any reading fixed by the configurations and actions of the first h steps that credits every renewing run credits some consuming run. The classification is a function neither of the initial configuration nor of any finite prefix. No ethical premise and no Lean axiom is used.

Canonical source: [Horizon.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Horizon.lean)

## 前提与对应 Hypotheses and correspondence

- 公地过程没有反馈：水平按汲取与更新逐步变化，起点可以任意高。 / The commons process has no feedback: the level changes by drawing and renewal at each step, and the starting level can be arbitrarily high.
- “读法”是运行上的任意命题；结论只要求它由前 h 步决定并记入每次更新运行。 / A “reading” is any proposition on runs; the conclusion requires only that it be fixed by the first h steps and credit every renewing run.

这是一个存在性结果：一个过程就足以说明有限前缀一般地不决定分类。在有反馈的过程中，越过阈值之后损失不会回来，但阈值之前的前缀是否仍可与及时停止的运行相同，没有证明。实际历史的视界与此的对应，是经验问题。 / This is an existence result: one process suffices to show that a finite prefix does not in general decide the classification. In processes with feedback, a loss past the threshold does not return, but whether a prefix before the threshold can still match a run that stops in time is not proved. The correspondence to the horizons of actual histories is an empirical question.
